surfaces.part: ramp dirt surface seen from above, descending away from viewer, with step/tread lines at rows 9, 14, 18-19, 22, 25, 27-28, 30
grass strips on both sides of the ramp

answer.evidence: The tile is a ramp seen almost straight down: a full-width brown dirt surface runs rows 0-31 with thin lighter tread lines (rows 9, 14, 18-19, 22, 25, 27-28, 30) and grass borders on the left and right. Dark cut edges (cliff walls) on both sides are narrow vertical strips, not a south face. There is no south-facing vertical front face of 3 or more rows. The ground surface fills the whole tile, so it reads as a top-down slab, which matches the described ramp viewed from above the terrace lip.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a stepped dirt ramp. Each tread has a light lip, a mid face and a dark riser shadow, which gives about 5 lightness steps on the brown ramp, plus grain dots on the treads. The measured facts support it: 11 visible tones per tile against 3 for the grass and 7 for the paving, and 0% near-flat coverage like both references. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the side walls and riser edges lean brown or green and read as dark tones of the neighbouring material, not a black sticker outline. Weaknesses: the treads are fairly regular and banded, and the texture is less varied than the grass clumps, so I rate it 'some', not 'rich'. It is still at or above the references on structure and density, and a careful artist would accept it beside them.
